name: BedrockEmbedding
title: Bedrock Embedding
description: Turn text into a vector using AWS Bedrock Titan models
whenToUse: Pick to turn a piece of text into the vector a similarity search needs, run on AWS in your own region and account. It embeds one text inline; offering embeddings to an attached agent on demand is a different node.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the text template

text.title: Text
text.description: The text to embed. Supports {{ signal.<id>.<handle>.<field> }}

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.description: Vector length. Must match what the store it goes into expects, or the search will reject it. v1 ignores this and always returns 1536.

normalize.title: Normalize
normalize.description: Scale to unit length, which is what cosine similarity expects

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.

package.name: aws-bedrock
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# BEDROCK AS MANIFESTS, and the cheapest AWS package to convert: both API calls it makes
# (Converse and InvokeModel) are plain signed JSON POSTs. Everything it needed already
# existed by the time it was reached — the signer from DynamoDB, and `transport: binary`
# for the attachments Claude can read.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/aws-bedrock/`.

name: aws-bedrock
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: Claude and GPT models plus Titan embeddings on AWS Bedrock
version: 2.1.0
category: ai
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749137717/gravity/icons/vdyfnijyuyk8ajqtp3nu.webp

features:
  - Claude on Bedrock via the native Messages API, with images, documents and tools
  - GPT on Bedrock, one prompt to one completion
  - Titan text embeddings, inline or over a service edge
  - Apply Bedrock guardrails to any text — screen, block or mask by your org's policy

# Two labels deep at least: bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com.
allowedHosts:
  - "**.amazonaws.com"
  # The bedrock-mantle endpoint, AWS's host for the native Anthropic Messages API:
  # bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws.
  - "**.api.aws"
  # Any host, for the UNAUTHENTICATED attachment fetches only. BedrockClaude reads an image
  # or document from a url a person supplies, which cannot be declared in advance. Those
  # calls send no credential, and the executor refuses "*" the moment one does.
  - "*"

requires:
  # SigV4 for the embeddings nodes; the LLM nodes authenticate with a Bedrock API key,
  # x-api-key on the Mantle endpoint and bearer on bedrock-runtime.
  credential: [awsSigV4, apiKeyHeader, bearer]
  transport: [json, binary]
  # Bedrock embeds ONE text per request, so a batch is a fan-out.
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.awsCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from plugin-base's shared AWSCredential, NAME AND FIELDS UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `awsCredential` keep resolving. Every AWS package
# shares this one, exactly as they shared the TypeScript definition.
#
# sessionToken is NEW, and additive. The retired definition had no such field, so anyone on
# temporary credentials (an assumed role, anything via STS) could not use these nodes at
# all. The signer sends and signs it only when it is filled in.

name: awsCredential
displayName: AWS Credentials
description: AWS credentials for AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, Bedrock, and the rest)
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html

properties:
  - name: accessKeyId
    displayName: Access Key ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Access Key ID
    placeholder: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
  - name: secretAccessKey
    displayName: Secret Access Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Secret Access Key
    placeholder: ""
  - name: region
    displayName: AWS Region
    type: string
    required: false
    default: us-east-1
    description: The region your tables live in
    placeholder: us-east-1
  - name: sessionToken
    displayName: Session Token
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: Only for temporary credentials from STS or an assumed role. Leave empty for a long-lived key.
    placeholder: ""
credentials.bedrockCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# A Bedrock API key, NOT an IAM access-key pair. Minted on the Bedrock console's API keys
# page, it authenticates as a plain header with no SigV4 signing: `x-api-key` against the
# bedrock-mantle Anthropic endpoint, `Authorization: Bearer` against bedrock-runtime.
#
# The embeddings nodes keep the signed awsCredential; this one belongs to the LLM nodes.

name: bedrockCredential
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: API key credentials for AWS Bedrock model calls
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: A Bedrock API key from the Bedrock console
    placeholder: ABSK...

  - name: region
    displayName: Region
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: The AWS region your Bedrock models are enabled in
    placeholder: us-east-1

shared.bedrock.yaml:
# The one call shape every Bedrock node makes.
#
# Bedrock is REST, unlike DynamoDB: the model id is in the PATH and the operation is the
# last segment, so there is no X-Amz-Target header here. `bedrock-runtime` is the signing
# service name and is NOT the same as the console's "bedrock" — signing against the wrong
# one is a 403 that says nothing about which name was wrong.

call: &call
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: awsSigV4
    service: bedrock-runtime
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  # Bedrock throttles hard under load and answers 429; retrying is the difference between a
  # workflow that survives a burst and one that fails a step at random.
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

host: &host >-
  return 'https://bedrock-runtime.' + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com'

# The same call, authenticated with a Bedrock API key instead of request signing.
# bedrock-runtime accepts the key as a plain bearer header, so the executor needs no
# signer for the nodes that use this shape.
keyCall: &keyCall
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.bedrockCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical Bedrock model lists, one per model family, organised by TIER.
#
# Same contract as openai/shared/models.yaml: the data lives here, the fallback logic
# (`resolve: modelTier` on the config field) lives in the executor. A new generation is
# a per-tier edit here, and every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# Bedrock ids carry the vendor prefix. Enable each model for your region in the Bedrock
# console before first use; that is an account setting, not something a manifest can do.

claude:
  # Listed large first so the strongest reads first. The picker's options.
  enum:
    - anthropic.claude-opus-5
    - anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
    - anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5

  # Version numbers in the labels by request. When a generation ships, the label is
  # edited alongside the id, or the two lie together.
  enumNames:
    - Claude Opus 5 (Frontier, complex work)
    - Claude Sonnet 5 (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - Claude Haiku 4.5 (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  # Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
  default: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

gpt:
  enum:
    - openai.gpt-5.6-sol
    - openai.gpt-5.6-terra
    - openai.gpt-5.6-luna

  enumNames:
    - GPT-5.6 Sol (Frontier, complex work)
    - GPT-5.6 Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - GPT-5.6 Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  default: openai.gpt-5.6-terra

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: embedding
  from: response
  value: "return Array.isArray(response.embedding) ? response.embedding : []"
files.api/run.yaml:
# One signed InvokeModel. The model id is in the PATH, so there is no header naming an
# operation the way DynamoDB needs one.

- $ref: bedrock#call
  name: embed
  url: >-
    return 'https://bedrock-runtime.' + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1')
      + '.amazonaws.com/model/' + encodeURIComponent(config.model) + '/invoke'
  body:
    inputText: "{{ config.text }}"
    # v1 rejects these two outright; v2 takes them. Sent only for the model that has them,
    # rather than trusting the vendor to ignore what it does not understand.
    dimensions: "return config.model === 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v1' ? undefined : (config.dimensions || 1024)"
    normalize: "return config.model === 'amazon.titan-embed-text-v1' ? undefined : (config.normalize !== false)"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [text]
  properties:
    text:
      type: string
      title: Text
      description: The text to embed. Supports {{ signal.<id>.<handle>.<field> }}
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      enum: [amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0, amazon.titan-embed-text-v1]
      enumNames: [Titan Text v2, Titan Text v1]
      default: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0
    dimensions:
      type: number
      title: Dimensions
      description: >-
        Vector length. Must match what the store it goes into expects, or the search will
        reject it. v1 ignores this and always returns 1536.
      enum: [1024, 512, 256]
      default: 1024
    normalize:
      type: boolean
      title: Normalize
      description: Scale to unit length, which is what cosine similarity expects
      default: true
      "ui:widget": toggle

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, text, model, dimensions, normalize]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the text template
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: embedding
    type: array
    description: The embedding vector

credentials:
  - name: awsCredential
    required: true
    displayName: AWS
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: BedrockEmbedding
kind: PromiseNode

name: Bedrock Embedding
category: AI
color: "#01A88D"

description: Turn text into a vector using AWS Bedrock Titan models

whenToUse: >-
  Pick to turn a piece of text into the vector a similarity search needs, run on AWS in your
  own region and account. It embeds one text inline; offering embeddings to an attached
  agent on demand is a different node.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Cacheable: the same text and model give the same vector, deterministically. This is one
  # of the few model calls where reuse is genuinely correct rather than merely cheaper.
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
    model: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0
    dimensions: 1024
    normalize: true
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    # The LENGTH is the assertion that matters: a vector of the wrong size is rejected by
    # whatever store it goes into, and "is an array" would pass on an empty one.
    embedding: "return output.embedding.length === 1024 && typeof output.embedding[0] === 'number'"
